title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results
abstract: We implement reference renewal to reconsider retained physical quantum-service results under a prespecified protocol. Twelve transitions retained six results each; ten completed renewal, eight met the prespecified endpoint, and five succeeded using retained results alone. The exact one-sided p=0.0546875 does not establish the recovery hypothesis. Incomplete references, binding failures and sequential waits expose operational limits. Offline reconstruction recovers decisions from preserved counts. Retrospective binding-plus-oracle checking accepts all 60 usable-transition results without renewal. With the exact oracle also supplying calibration scores, the study does not demonstrate incremental numerical-correctness utility of renewal.
comment: 23 pages, 3 figures. Supplementary material (14 pages; ESM_1.pdf) is available as an ancillary file. Submitted to Quantum Information Processing, Quantum Software Engineering collection. Numerical artifact (ESM_2.zip) and reproducibility archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24108573

bite.hook: Study finds 'reference renewal'—re-checking quantum service results—fails to provide clear numerical-correctness gains.
tldr: Researchers tested whether re-evaluating retained quantum-service results (reference renewal) improves the reliability of the final output.
They compared renewal protocols against oracle-based checking across 60 transition results.
The results showed that renewal did not provide significant incremental utility compared to simpler oracle-based verification.
bite.whyItMatters: As quantum services move to the cloud, we need to know if complex verification protocols are actually worth the extra computational cost.
bite.eli5: Imagine you solve a math problem and then re-check your work using a complicated second method. If the second method doesn't actually catch any new mistakes or make the answer more certain, it's just a waste of time. This study suggests that for quantum results, this 're-checking' might not be helping.
